lines.text: God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor but does not let him enjoy them, so a stranger does.
A man may father a hundred children and live many years, yet a stillborn child is better off than he.
The stillborn child never sees the sun, yet has more joy than the man who lives a thousand years twice over.
All a man's labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.
No one knows what is good for a man during the few days he passes through life like a cloud.
